utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm glad to see you back, Mr. Martinovic. I hope you're feeling better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krsnik, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, and thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would -- consistent with the Chamber's practices, we'd ask to receive copies of all documents that will be used during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any documents, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as regards the practices of this Court and as regards what has been allowed to the Prosecution, at the moment we are going to be using documents during the cross-examination. We shall be providing them to the Prosecution. And the documents that we have now, we can give them to the -- my learned friend immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we have many documents, we are sure that we are going to be using the ones that we have just given the Prosecution. And as for the rest, we shall see during the cross-examination. Your Honours, I would just like to inform you that many of these documents are those that we have received from our learned friend on the 4th of October, so a few days ago. So many of them have not been translated, but some of them are very short. And with the assistance of our interpreters, I believe we will be able to present the exhibits to the witness. But at the same time, I would also like to say that there are a number of documents which have been translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me introduce myself. I'm counsel Kresimir Krsnik, acting on behalf of Mr. Naletilic as his Defence counsel. I'm going to ask you a few questions. Please bear in mind that we speak the same language, and whatever you and I say is interpreted into two languages. I would like to ask you to speak slowly and make a pause between my question and your answer.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, before I start asking you about details, can you please clarify something that confused me yesterday. You confused me when you said the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I never heard that expression before. So can you explain the term "the Armed Forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina." And then can you please clarify your position. That was another thing that you confused me with. First tell me who and what are the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the decree which was issued in 1992, it says that the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina are composed of the Territorial Defence at the very beginning and then the Croatian Defence Council, MUP units, if that was necessary. But in practical terms, at the time the Armed Forces were composed of all those who were prepared to fight for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Looking at the transcript -- but if I understand you well, the Armed Forces were the TO and the HVO, the Territorial Defence and the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please come closer to the microphone. Thank you. And the HVO as such were the legal armed or military force of the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The HVO according to that decree was a legitimate force for the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, probably until the moment when it started attacking that same Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We will come to that. And I hope we will be able to establish who attacked whom and who was it who attacked Bosnia and Herzegovina. When you say "attack Bosnia and Herzegovina," are you referring to conflicts within Bosnia and Herzegovina, or is maybe an attack on Bosnia and Herzegovina the attack of the BH Army on Boksevica, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honour. It's beyond the scope of the direct examination and beyond the scope of the rebuttal testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krsnik, there's too wide a range of the cross-examination. Try to limit your cross-examination in two aspects: One is the credibility of this witness. The other is the Rados diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have hardly started, and already my learned friend is objecting. Your Honours, the credibility of a witness is this question. I have not even finished the question. I have not even said what I wanted to say, and already my learned friend objects and already I am being warned. Your Honours, if somebody in this courtroom mentions the Armed Forces, then I want this to be clarified. It goes for the credibility. We know what we have been hearing in this courtroom for a year or so, and now the witness says that the HVO started attacking. I would like to clarify. Who was it who -- that the HVO attacked? Is an attack on Bosnia and Herzegovina, if the BH Army attacks one village and the HVO attacks another village? Does that mean that both attacked Bosnia and Herzegovina? I would like to find out what the witness thinks. An allocation cannot just stay lingering in the air. This is the first time we have heard of the Armed Forces. We are aware of the BH Army. We are aware of the HVO. We are aware of the Republika Srpska Army. But for the first time we hear of the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's what I wanted to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I've already said that these things have been in dispute from the very beginning to almost the last day of the trial. I know your position on that issue, and I also know the positions of the Prosecutor. But this matter has nothing to do with the credibility of the witness and there is nothing to do with the Rados diary. This is a cross-examination. I hope you could concentrate your cross-examination on these two main points rather than engaging in some debates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to engage in any debates. Can you please leave me and witness to do our job. I know what the purpose of my cross-examination is. I know it very well. I am well prepared for this cross-examination. We all need to hear what this witness has to say. And when he has something, I have the right to clarify his words. I have hardly started my cross-examination; we have already wasted ten minutes on a debate. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said to the Prosecutor yesterday that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina -- when he said the Muslim Army, you corrected him and said, "No, that is the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Can you please tell me in addition to Jovan Divjak -- General Divjak and General Stjepan Siber, can you give me the name of one Serb or one Croat who were in the army in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gladly. In front of me I have the booklet containing the names of fallen soldiers in Jablanica. Two Croats and one Serb are mentioned. If necessary, the book is here and I will find the pages containing the photos and the personal data of those three soldiers. You cannot imply that all the armies in Bosnia and Herzegovina were ethically pure. The HVO was not ethically pure at the beginning. When the HVO decided to attack the areas which were not under its control, the first thing it did, it ethically cleansed its own units. But since you say that you are well prepared, you know what the HVO did with the Muslims --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, sir.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It is me who leads this testimony, not you.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, will you allow me --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I am kindly asking you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now, I think both of you have to calm down. Witness, did you finish your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't, Mr. President. I thought that I would be given the time to say something to Mr. Krsnik. What I wanted to say is that I will gladly answer all of his questions, but once he asks me something, I would like him to give me the time to answer that question as I want. Please, if I may be given the time and if please can the counsel let me answer the question that he puts to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I lead the cross-examination here. Everybody knows it. And witness, I am the one who will be asking questions and you will answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. The Chamber will recall on many, many occasions the Prosecution was required to listen to long, non-responsive answers from many Defence witnesses. When I objected and when I tried to draw the witness's attention to giving a response of a more responsive question, I was repeatedly told to give -- let the witness answer. So I think the same treatment should be afforded to the Prosecution witnesses as was afforded to the Defence witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, try to finish your answer in a very concise and short way so that we can move on. I think if Defence counsel needs more information in this aspect, he will ask you more questions in that direction. Yes. You may finish your answer, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to say is when the HVO decided to, the first thing it did, it sent all the Muslims from its units to camps. This is what we didn't do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We will come to that, witness, very soon and we will have evidence to show you. So we've established that you had two Serbs and one Croat.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What year was that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two in 1993 and one in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. Then can you tell me, you come from the village of Dobrigosce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did Serbs in Jablanica have an independent military association in 1992 or 1993? Were they organised?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to relevance beyond the scope of direct, beyond the scope of the rebuttal case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think I've mentioned that you could ask some questions in cross-examination in two areas: One is the credibility of this witness; the other is the Rados diary. This is the main purpose of the cross-examination. We don't have to come from 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yesterday the year 1992 was mentioned on direct, and there was also questions about independent Serbian units. And I have just had confirmation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm interested in the native village of Mr. Safet Idrizovic, Dobrigosce. Tell me, in your village, what was the ethnic composition of the population there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is at all important, there was an equal percentage of Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell me something about the lot of the Serbs. Are there any Serbs in Dobrigosce today? Have there been any since 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They abandoned the village in 1994 after the signing of the agreement between Croats and Muslims when the Federation was established. And I believe that their political structures decided that as many people as possible should leave the area of the Federation. At the time they probably thought that they wouldn't be able to live there. That's why they left the village. After the signing of that agreement, I believe that it was the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What you're saying now you're saying under oath.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They left in 1994 because of the political circumstances relative to the establishment of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina because at the time it was called a Muslim Croat Federation and they didn't find themselves there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: None of the houses were touched. None of them were burned down.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They all remained. They're all intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who lives in those houses?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You personally, did you establish a special unit there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's a very small village, and it is on the verge of disappearance. It is a small village very high up in the mountain, and before the war it was one of the most -- least densely populated villages in the area. People normally emigrated into towns. And the total number of military conscripts in the village was less than ten, so there were no conditions in place to establish a military unit, even the smallest one. And I didn't live in that village. I hadn't lived there for a long time before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please tell me who killed Duro Manigoda, or maybe I should go on mentioning the names of the villagers of that village.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The criminals?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Duro Manigoda was a rich man, and he was killed by criminals who wanted to get hold of his money. There was an investigation against these people. And when the law on amnesty was passed in Bosnia, then those people were amnestied, like many other criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Criminals in the Army of BH or others?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the criminals. A criminal is a criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I agree with you. Were you also in Duro Manigoda's house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Immediately after his murder.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did his daughter find you in his courtyard?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please ask the counsel and the witness to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we have a problem of the interpretation. You have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that. [Interpretation] Certainly I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's try and clarify one other thing: Your position from 26 October, 1992 until the end of 1993, can you please tell us exactly what you were. What was your position in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I was very precise yesterday when I described my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You were the chief of the BH Army staff for Jablanica municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was the commander of the defence staff for the army in Jablanica. I was not the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: See, we have to clarify. You were the commander of the BH Army for Jablanica municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official title was the commander of the Armed Forces of Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: See, we need to clarify things. We will very soon be able to communicate very well. We need clarifications. And that is what you did until the end of 1993. I'm interested in 1993. I'm not interested in the period after that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will repeat what I said yesterday. I was the commander of the staff of the Armed Forces of Jablanica from 28th of October, 1992, until the end of January 1994. That is, the signing of the agreement on the establishment of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, I already said that at the end of 1992 or early 1993 I received an order from my superior commander, Mr. Pasalic, to establish in Jablanica a brigade and to place it under the command which will then be a part of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember your first statement that you gave in the year 2000? In the year 2000 you gave a statement - on the 12th of July, it was - do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In that statement you say -- and if you say this is not correct, I'm going to show it to you. But I now want to avoid wasting time. "Around the 26th of October, 1992, the staff of the BH Army in Sarajevo removed Salko Zerim from the position of chief of the staff of the Armed Forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Jablanica. General Sefer Halilovic the main commander in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina appointed me to replace Salko Zerim and that position was the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina." This is your statement.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slowly. I believe that it was a bad translation. The position of the Chief of Staff was the second position. The first position is the commander. The second position is Chief of Staff. Salko Zerim was not the Chief of Staff. He was the commander, and I replaced him in that position. There must have been a mistake either in typing or in translation, but this is not important. From then onwards I was the main person within that command structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If I -- my memory serves me well, your first function was the Chief of Staff. That was Sefer Halilovic. He was the Chief of Staff of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he was the commander. In the army structure, the commander is above the chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That is later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You forget yourself, Mr. Krsnik. Try to slow down so that the interpretation can catch up with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I agree with you more or less. We won't enter into a debate, because this happened at a subsequent date, when Rasim Delic appeared. He was the commander, and someone else was the chief. But it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you were the main person in the BH Army in Jablanica; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that was the case up until the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You haven't allowed me to answer your question. I said that I was ordered to form a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell us when.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I finished with that task on the 21st of January, 1993. From that date onwards, the brigade entered the corps and it was under the command of Mr. Pasalic. The staff of the Armed Forces remained as a body. I remained at the head of that staff, but my duties did not cover the same area. I had less responsibility, and it involved providing security for important buildings in the area of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that was all that you as the chief of the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina did in 1993. You only provided security for buildings, as is the case with the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Civilian protection has certain responsibilities. The civilian protection is not an armed force. It has no weapons, and it doesn't provide security for buildings in any countries. I believe that it doesn't do this in Croatia either. The task of the civilian protection is to save people and property, to protect them from bad weather conditions, to protect them in war conditions, and to protect them from other disasters. Buildings -- security for buildings are provided by -- is provided by armed people in peacetime and in wartime. And I believe that is the case in Croatia now too. I believe that people with weapons provide security for buildings. I think you would agree with me, that that is the case in Croatia too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I know that you're a professor of national defence and national protection. I know that you're an expert on this matter. However, that is not the case. Perhaps it is the case in the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but that is not the case in Croatia. Nevertheless, I'm interested in the number of people you had under you as the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the command?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, the command.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were about 200 people. And just let me add this: These people were between the age of 50 and 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. So you are telling us that after January 1993 you were not in a position to issue orders to anyone. You weren't in a position to plan, to provide logistical operations. What did you do then were you only involved in protecting buildings? Could you have arrested someone, for example?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's all. That's all we did. We had people who provided security for the command and the hydroelectric powerplants were -- they provided security for hydroelectric powerplants, special purposes industry, the military hospital, the war hospital, important bridges, important railway bridges, the water supply system these are the facilities that they provided security for. Up until the beginning of July -- I don't have the time to explain all this to the Court, to explain the purpose of establishing the brigade and the staff. Perhaps people don't understand what the two of us are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, that is a problem in general here at the Tribunal, but we'll come that. We'll make an effort and you will try and help me to clarify certain issues. I asked you whether you as a commander were in a position to arrest and imprison someone, for example.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every commander had the possibility of doing that. Naturally in the area -- in the part that was his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me please: Who were you protecting this hydroelectric powerplant from? And so that the Trial Chamber can understand you, since you said that the enemy never entered the territory of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could now put your question. But no, I'll answer the question. It's not a problem. I was then in charge of the security at the hydroelectric powerplant. I now have 60 people who provide security and they're armed with pistols. I could now ask you who were they protecting this powerplant from. From criminals? From thieves? I don't know from whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But what sort of special purposes industry did you have there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had an industry. It's not a secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, what did you produce?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We produced mortar shells, small-calibre mortar shells, 60 and 82 millimetre mortar shells. This is no secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, who provided the BH Army with logistics support? Wasn't that the task of the staff of the Armed Forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour. I object to relevance. Beyond the scope of direct examination. Completely beyond anything we talked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think you spent a lot of time and questions on credibility of this witness already. And some of the questions are related to that issue. But this one, I didn't see any relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry to hear that, Mr. President, but as far as the credibility of the witness is concerned, I haven't even started yet. I haven't even started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you have to move on. We don't have the whole day for you to cross-examine this witness, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know I don't have the whole day to cross-examine this witness. I know all of that. But I can't forget that I'm in a court, a war crimes tribunal, and we all want this -- the proceedings to be fair and just. You know, there is nothing that I want to conceal here. I need to establish a basis. We have to determine what the witness said yesterday and then what he said in the year 2000. We have to compare these two things. We found out that he wasn't the Chief of Staff in the municipality, which is what was claimed yesterday. So let's determine what his responsibility was, because in the subsequent events that unfolded in 1993 the figure of Mr. Idrizovic is of key importance in Jablanica and the events that took place in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what they say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But actually, who provided the BH Army with logistics support? I don't think this question is relevant. Mr. Krsnik, you have to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with all due respect, I can't agree with you. You interrupt me in advance. You know why it's important. Your Honours, it's important because -- the witness will confirm this under oath; that's for sure -- a thousand of soldiers came from outside of Jablanica, and Croats were expelled from their homes so that they could be accommodated. I have a list of their names. And the gentleman here is aware of this, because at the time he was a commander. You know, Mr. President -- can you see what's happening to me in the course of my cross-examination? How am I supposed to conduct it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I know that, you know, this witness was an eyewitness to many, many events that happened in that area, but that is not the scope of the rebuttal proceeding. In the cross-examination the rebuttal proceeding should be strictly limited to two areas: One is the credibility of this witness; two is the Rados diary. That's quite clear, you know. You don't have to ask all the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I don't have to ask a single question. I know how I'm conducting this examination. How am I to get to the diary of Alojz Rados if I don't prepare the terrain? Shall I just ask a few questions? Shall we be satisfied with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in the cross-examination, especially in the rebuttal proceedings, I have already said that you could ask some leading questions, directly lead this witness to the particular question you want to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, the special detachment for special purposes of the staff of the command of the BH forces, under Zulfikar Alispago -- this was accommodated in a house in Jablanica in Zuka Rogic's house, Mato Krtic, Mato Bilos, Andelko Rogic, Josip Brekalo, Marinko Brekalo, Mile Pjaca and many others -- I was going a bit too fast. I apologise. I'll have to repeat these names, because they haven't entered the transcript. And the first question didn't enter the transcript either, the question I put to you a minute ago. I'll try and repeat it slowly. The units that we will call "Zuka's Units," and their name is the "Special detachment for special purposes in the staff of the Supreme Command of the BH Army." The Zulfikar Alispago, also known as Zuka. His men, his units were billeted in Rogic's house in Donja Jablanica, is that correct? Your answer was?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But no one else in Jablanica had anything to do with that. Mr. President, the special detachment for special purposes in the staff of the Supreme Command, Mr. Krsnik has to know that it's a detachment that was formed by the staff of the Supreme Command for special purposes and they sent it to Jablanica. Why are you asking me about that detachment? That's a detachment of the staff of the Supreme Command. At the time the army was under the command of Sefer Halilovic. When he comes to this Tribunal and proceedings have been instituted against him, ask Mr. Halilovic who formed and with what purpose this detachment and why it was sent to Jablanica. I don't know the answer. All I do know is that the Croats had problems with the soldiers from that unit, but we did too, to the same extent as the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All I wanted to ask you -- and we have to move on, because we're in a hurry -- is did Sefer Halilovic billet them in Rogic's house in Donja Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I can't answer that question as to whether Sefer billeted them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who provided them with logistics support? Who gave them those houses?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were formed by the staff of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, please, who billeted them in Rogic's house? That's the municipality which was under your command. Who gave them those houses, and what happened with the Croats who were in those houses?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my municipality, and I was the commander, but I told you what I was the commander of at that time and those peoples -- the units were such that they didn't need anything. They took what they needed themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. We should have said that at the beginning. Let's move on now. Tell me please, what units for special purpose, called the Crni Labudovi, "the Black Swans," accommodated in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were never there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The Hunter Division?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: "Silver Fox"?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Silver Fox" -- let's just wait for the interpretation to finish. "Silver Fox," well, it consisted of about ten soldiers. Sometimes they would come from Igman, when it was taken by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The so-called "Celo's People", were they in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Celo's People" weren't in Jablanica. They were in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. What about the "Igman Wolves," or the so-called "Cedo's Wolves"? Were they in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation. Yes, but this was a small group of men, about ten people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many men did the BH Army have in Jablanica in total? How many men did they have at their disposal?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you about the units from Jablanica. Don't ask me anything about units from outside of Jablanica. We were afraid -- we were terrified by those people. You probably know why. You know what sort of people they might have been, the sort of people who went all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't know. Please tell the Court.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I won't go into that. I had about 200 people between the age of 50 and 60, and there were up to 2.000 people in our brigade. I'm talking about the 44th Mountain Brigade. And these are the men from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you're telling me that you were not in a position to exert an influence when the people from these units that I have mentioned passed through Jablanica in their armoured vehicles and they shot from their weapons, they looted flats and shops. You were not in a position to do anything about this.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we had been armoured vehicles, that would have been good. Unfortunately we didn't have such vehicles. They didn't have such vehicles either. I've told you that all these small units were minor ones. It's not important to mention them. Cedo's Wolves, et cetera, there were about up to 25 men in them. Please. I haven't finished. I'm waiting for the interpretation. I haven't finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I understand. That is clear.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're nervous. I was nervous yesterday. You're nervous today. All those minor units are of no importance. Zuka's Unit, the one you call Zuka's Unit - that's what we called it too - their name show that is they weren't under the command of the corps. If it's a special detachment of the staff of the Supreme Command, then the staff of the Supreme Command commands them, not the corps command. And you're asking me whether I, who had 200 old men, whether I was a leader there. But there were 400 of Zuka's men there. I really don't know whether you understand these military matters. I don't know whether you know what you want to ask. Did you think that I was in a position to issue orders to Zuka, that Zuka was under my command?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No. I know that you didn't command Zuka. But I know that you provided logistics support when he was in the area of your movement you helped him and all the unit that is came to the territory of your municipality. But tell me, Mato Krtic, Mato Bilos, Josip Brekalo, Marinko Brekalo, Mile Pjaca, Andelko Rogic -- yes, I won't waste time now. We shall later on deal with the names. I think they'll come to ask me for the names that I have just mentioned. It wasn't all the same to them, the fact that they had been expelled from their houses in order to make room for the units. I could also mention many people from whom their cars had been taken for the purposes of these units so that these units could use them. And you -- are you going to tell this Trial Chamber that you are not aware of this fact or you are aware of this fact? Is it true? Is it not true?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was I aware of this or not? Why is this important? Of what pertinence is it for this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just tell me, is that true what I said? Is it true to say that these people were expelled from their homes in order to make room for these units?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period that you are referring to, there were between 9 and 10 thousand refugees in Jablanica. Jablanica is a small town and has about 3.000 inhabitants. So you can well imagine a situation in Zagreb, which has about a million inhabitants, if another 3 million inhabitants appear, you can imagine that sort of situation in Zagreb, what sort of a Zagreb would that be. What would it look like? It was a beehive, and it was impossible to pass through it. Units from the outside had weapons and they were armed far better than we were, ten times better than we were. We didn't have the responsibility and we didn't have the possibility to control the way in which Zuka's men behaved. Please, if they are guilty - and I do believe that they caused problems - then the relevant Prosecution offices should institute proceedings against those people. It's not a problem at all. Please, just a minute. I respect you, but you will have to respect me too. I've now lost the thread of my thought. I don't know what I wanted to say. We weren't in a position to control Zuka's men and no one was responsible for them. And even if my -- I wouldn't feel sorry for anyone, even if it were my own brother, if that person committed a crime, he should be held responsible for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask. Did Zuka's men cause problems or did they commit crimes? You've just said what you were thinking, so let's move on now. Tell me, did you have the right to arrest people and put them in the camp that was formed in Jablanica around 15 of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I believe this question is totally irrelevant of the subject matter of the rebuttal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't ask any questions about the camp. My question was whether the gentleman here could arrest somebody and send them to that camp. And it goes to the credibility. And I believe that this is relevant. That's why I'm asking the gentleman whether he himself personally had the right to arrest people and send them to the camp. I have statements here given to the Prosecutors of this Court mentioning this gentleman and mentioning such facts. These statements were given to the investigators of this Tribunal. Maybe the gentleman is not aware of that. I'm going to show them this -- the statements, if the Prosecution hasn't done that already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Even if it's mentioned in the statement but it was not mentioned in the direct examination, it has nothing to do with the Rados diary. We have to move fast. I think you have spent a lot of time, over an hour, on the credibility of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is all interlinked. On his direct he said that all he did was providing security for the facilities. I believe that this is not the truth. This is a very important witness, and you must allow me to do my job. Please, Your Honours, if he only provided security for the facilities, then who put people into the camp? Not only on the 15th of April. Who placed guards around the camp? Who had control over that camp? And we haven't even started talking about Doljani. And when you hear what happened there, then we will still talk about the credibility and we will find out why Rados's diary is important, when it was fabricated, and why. But you have to bear with me, and it all goes to the credibility. And the questions about Alojz Rados's diary are prepared, but just allow me to ask a few questions that go to the credibility. Please allow me to lead this questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question again to you, sir, was: Whether you arrested people on the 15th of April, together with Hasan Hindic? Did you arrest them? Did you put them in the camp? Please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew you would ask me this. On the 15th of April, around 12.30, the shelling of Jablanica started. We were confused at first, disbelief, and then we started realising that aggression started. At the time we did not have any lines, defence lines towards the HVO, because on the 15th of April the HVO -- a year before that the HVO encircled us, surrounded us. We were sitting together with Mr. Kovacevic, the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot control the witness. I asked him a very simple question. The question was whether he arrested people on the 15th of April and send them to prison. I cannot stop him now.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you. Just let me talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a cooperative witness. He is answering my question. I cannot interrupt him. I have all the time in the world.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have all the time in the world as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I -- there's something else I wish to say. Is this a courtroom, Your Honour? Is the public area also a courtroom, the area behind the glass partition? If that is the courtroom - and I believe that it is, because people rise when you enter the court - I am not going to tolerate the laughter of this gentleman who is sitting in the public gallery. This is a journalist, and I cannot tolerate his behaviour. Can you please warn him to behave properly in the courtroom or to leave the courtroom. I can -- will not tolerate this behaviour. This is very disturbing, and I'm very confused. Whenever I look in that direction, I can see the gentleman who is behaving improperly in the courtroom, and I believe this is not the way to behave in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please warn this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you know that as a principle, that all the trials should be conducted in public hearing, and everybody is entitled to sit in the public gallery. Of course at the same time - at the same time - all those participants in the public gallery should refrain themselves from some extraordinary behaviour. But from my point of view, I didn't see any abnormal behaviour shown in the public gallery. If something happens in the public gallery, I believe the guard in charge of the security of that area could interfere. And in the past cases, they usually interfere in all those matters. Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You know, in some domestic jurisdictions, the experienced Defence counsel will face all kinds of problems from the public galleries. There will be shouting, laughing, cursing. I -- I understand that, you know, as a very experienced lawyer, you could cope with all these problems. At the same time, I'll inform the security guard in the public gallery to take care of the order in that area. But you have to concentrate on your cross-examination. As for your questions, Mr. Krsnik, I really don't think it's relevant to this very case. This witness is called only on the very limited scope, that is, the Rados diary. In the direct examination, allowed the Prosecutor to establish this witness. In the cross-examination, we allowed you to ask some questions concerning the credibility of this witness. Anyway, we have to come to the subject matter of these proceedings. He's not an ordinary witness. He's a rebuttal witness. We have to limit the scope of the direct examination, as well as the cross-examination. I understand you have been working very hard recently. And if you feel you have to reorganise your questions, we could have a break here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I am well prepared, and I don't see a problem. On the contrary. I shall then focus on the diary. I have a lot of questions about the diary. But then we will come back to the relevant issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So let's talk about the diary, sir. But I will come back to all the issues that I've tackled so far. When did you personally -- but just personal knowledge. You are under oath. What did you personally see? When did you personally see the diary for the first time and who was it who gave it the name "Alojz Rados's diary"?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said when I saw it for the first time. I said that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the so-called original.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it yesterday, but I'll repeat. It was on the 30th of July, 1993, late in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who showed it to you? Who brought it to you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Zajko Sihirlic, the security officer of the 44th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber what is the role of the security officer in a brigade.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the armies in the world have security officers. They have them in Croatia. They have them in America. They have them in the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm asking about Mr. Sihirlic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He performed the duties of the security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What duties are those?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He provided security for the units, for the command, safe keeping documents, safe keeping secret documents. Do you know what security in the army is? Everything that has to do with security is his duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Isn't that intelligence and counterintelligence, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish we had had such services, but we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You didn't?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. We were a newly established army. Maybe there was such a thing at a higher level. But at the municipal level, we didn't have that. We had officers for security with commands, and that is all we had as regards security, just officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I have in front of me something that I'm going to show you later on, and it is your letter to the intelligence organ of the 4th Corps that you just said you didn't have.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that they were such things at higher levels. I was not a member of a higher level command. But I also said --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please let me finish. Do you want my answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the command of the Armed Forces -- in the staff of the Armed Forces, there was an intelligence officer for security. But that is what you are implying, isn't that? I know what you're implying. I know what you want to ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it because you mentioned the report on security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please. Hold on please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't born yesterday, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please be so kind, tell us whether you were ever involved in intelligence or counterintelligence.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This is your letter on the 21st of January, 1993. This is what you say in your letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the usher's assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is D1/416.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Which, Mr. President, is not translated, so unfortunately it's not going to be much use to the Chamber or to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would you be so kind to take this in for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what you say. I'm interested in the last paragraph only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could somebody read that last paragraph so that we could get interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. I just wanted the gentleman to read it first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But first, Mr. Krsnik. First you have to ask a question whether this is the letter the witness wrote on a certain date. Then ask the witness to read the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: First of all, tell us what the title of this report signed by you is and who was it sent to.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to the intelligence organ of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell us the title of this report.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Intelligence report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It was submitted by who?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was submitted by the intelligence officer, and I signed it as a commander. I signed all the documents -- Stela is laughing at you. The intelligence order security report are sent every day at a certain hour from a subordinate to a superior. This was the last day I was responsible for that area of responsibility, that is, the 21st of January, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So every day -- every organ of a lower command at a certain time submitted a report to its superior in the superior command. Obviously I checked every document, and I signed it. That was the procedure. I believe such a procedure exists all over the world, that a commander signs the documents that leave his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, I'm not attacking you. You don't have to defend yourself. I'm just asking you questions, and all you have to do is tell us the truth.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't feel attacked -- being attacked. I don't have that feeling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm asking you very nicely. You told us a minute ago that you were not a member of the intelligence, that you didn't have intelligence in Jablanica, and all of a sudden you personally write an intelligence report and sign it.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat my answer again. You're wasting everybody's time here, sir. What I told you was that at a lower level in the command there were officers for intelligence matters and officers for security matters. Please don't interrupt me, because you're going to ask me the same question for the fourth time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Does the title say "intelligence reporting" and does it bear your signature?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was precise before, and I'm going to repeat my answer. An intelligence organ of a lower command sends a report to his superior command every day. Please, I need to clarify this. I don't want to go over the same grounds ten times. I need to clarify it for you. Nobody can put a stamp on a document which leaves any command if that document hasn't been signed by the commander of that commander or the person authorised by him. I believe you understand that. Those are basics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell us, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are these your words: "By the establishment of the command of the 4th Corps, this is the first official document --" I'm reading the last sentence -- "regarding the intelligence information. That is why we are kindly asking for your advice and instructions for our further work." Are these your words, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they are. But at this moment, please give me the time to answer. I haven't finished.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm moving on, sir.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the way we can play this game? I didn't answer your question. I didn't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You have, sir.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, let the witness finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that I had receive a document from the Corps Command, which probably was of intelligence nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's why I am asking you, because you said it didn't exist there.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. For the fifth time I have to repeat the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please don't. Let's move on. Zajko Sihirlic was one of those officers.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not "Zahilic" but "Sihirlic." And not intelligence but security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: He was the one who brought you the diary. Who was it you gave it to him? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me -- and I said it yesterday -- he told me that the military police came by the HVO documents, amongst which was the private diary written by our work colleague by the name of Alojz Rados.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please assist us and give the witness the alleged 928C. Witness, can you please tell us, where does it say that? Does it say anywhere that this is a diary?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything in the world has a name. This booklet must have a name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who gave it the name?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose the one who entered things by the dates, in a chronological order, and I believe that in Croatian, in Bosnian, in Serbian a booklet containing entries in a chronological order, describing events that took place in that chronological order, is called a diary. Who was it who invented that name, I really don't know, but a name has to be given to this thing. This paper has its title, and the title is "Intelligence reporting." This booklet also. If you were the one reading it -- let me ask you a question in return: If you came by a booklet like this, and if I was its author, how would you call this booklet?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What would I call it? That doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. This is a man's personal diary. It's a diary. It's not a novel. It's not a drama. It's not a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, it seems to me that it's a minor issue in this case, whether it's a diary or not is not that important. The most important is its source, authenticity, the contents in it. You don't have to ask the witness to agree with you. Can we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please tell whose handwriting is it. Who wrote it in their hand that this is Alojz Rados's diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the Exhibit 928, that is, the copy that has been provided to us by Mr. Idrizovic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't bother. I don't remember who was it who wrote it down. But if it -- if it had been me and if I had been the one who had to give it a title, I would have probably done the same. I believe that you would have done the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That is true. But the allegations so far is somewhat different, so this is something I need to clarify. So this handwritten title "Alojz Rados," this is not his own handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. So that's good. In your statement given in 2000, you said something completely different. You said something like this: Around the 27th of July, 1993, in the evening -- but I cannot remember the date for a fact -- the 44th Brigade of the BH Army liberated the village of Doljani -- liberated. In the HVO staff of Doljani, BH Army members discovered a number of HVO documents and brought it to the BH Army staff in Jablanica. That is to you. This is what you stated on the 12th of July, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could Mr. Krsnik please indicate for purposes of this and in fairness to the witness, could Mr. Krsnik please put to the witness that part of that statement which is inconsistent with what he just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik, would you please put that statement to the witness just to be fair to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. We are approaching the break, I believe, so I'm going to give this statement to the witness, both in Croatian and in English. And the purpose of this question is to show that Mr. Idrizovic is inconsistent in his statement and -- but we are now coming to the break, so maybe we can stop here and then I can continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, to -- to avoid other problems that we've had this week, I'm going to ask that if we're going to go into these statements, that the copies of the statement be provided to the Court. Otherwise, I -- we're going to get into the situation we did the other day and I fear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Mr. Krsnik, if you don't have extra copies, I think during the break Madam Registrar will have them copied. So we will break now, and we will resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry to do this now, but it seems that we always -- at the end of the break, we always move out of the courtroom rather quickly and I don't want to forget. I don't expect you to tell me in open court, of course. But I do want to just remind the Chamber that we have not at this time still been advised of who Witness X is. We have no information about this person, or if the person is still coming, or whoever it is. We have no information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, concerning Mr. X, I think this Trial Chamber made a decision that -- which requested you to furnish the summaries of that witness to the Prosecution yesterday. Just tell us, you know, whether he's coming or not, or did you fulfil your obligation according to this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we discuss the matter of this witness later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to request this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I have some new information which I wanted to present to you today, but I wouldn't like to do so in open session and at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I do want to confirm that I didn't comply with your order yesterday, and this is just so as to respond to the Prosecutor. I think that I was supposed to provide certain indications, certain summaries, by yesterday. I didn't do that, and I admit that. This shall be provided today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll not discuss this issue, especially when the witness is present. You may continue your cross-examination. And after we finish this witness, you may give us more information on that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. We were discussing your statement that you gave in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we provide the witness with a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It's on page -- we call the language B/C/S here. We call it the B/C/S version here. It's on page 24. Could you go to page 24, please -- 25. I apologise. Page 25. You see the first paragraph, the second, the third -- "About the 23rd of July," have you found that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Here you say, "Around the 27th of July, 1993. I can't remember the exact date. The 44th Brigade of the ABiH liberated the village of Doljani. In the HVO headquarters in Doljani, members of the 44th Brigade of the ABiH discovered a large number of documents belonging to the HVO and they brought them to the ABiH staff in Jablanica." And then you continue. "Before we handed over the HVO documents that we found in the course of the action in Doljani, before we hand them over to the legal authorities of the ABiH, we made copies of the documents that concerned the municipality of Jablanica. I did this in order to be sure that none of the documents would be lost or would disappear. I still have copies of these documents, and I will hand them over to the representatives of the Prosecution at the ICTY." Did you make such a statement?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can we say that what you said here is not correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To an extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now tell me, do you personally know who had the diary in his hands for the first time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zajko Sihirlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Could counsel indicate which part of the statement just read is inconsistent with what the witness has testified here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that Mr. Krsnik will ask some more questions in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik already said at line 12, he said, "Can we say that what you said is not correct." And the answer was, "To an extent." None of us in the courtroom know what it is about those three or four paragraphs that are supposedly inconsistent with what the witness has testified here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that Mr. Krsnik will pursue on that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was going to move on to the diary because I think that it is very clear as to what is inconsistent. What I have read out doesn't correspond to what the witness said at the hearing.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is why I wanted to know whether what is said in the statement is correct. Did the witness make this claim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is it correct? To a certain extent he said it wasn't correct; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some translation errors, I think. I didn't have the opportunity to sign this statement in my own language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In what language did you sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, an interpreter read it out to me in English. I can't remember exactly what happened in the year 2000, but I think that that is what happened. When the investigators took the statement -- after they had taken it, the interpreter would read it out. Usually when these documents are read they're interpreted twice, and many things get lost in the translation. So in these four paragraphs there are certain details that are not precise and not correct. If necessary, I shall clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me lead you. You said that they were found by members of the military police. Here you say, "Members of the 44th Brigade of the ABiH." Just a minute, please. You said that the military police first found the documents, and today you said Zajko Sihirlic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the military police, but I said that Zajko Sihirlic was the first person to have the diary in his hands. He was the first person to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, did you say the military police or the members of the 44th Brigade? I can't understand how this can be incorrectly translated.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the statement that I gave earlier on I stated in very precise terms that part of Doljani had been liberated by some of the units from the 44th Mountain Brigade. I also said that the military police that had authority at the time were -- the military police were those who entered the command first and they found the documents there. Naturally, it's not their task. It's not the police's task to read documents. Their task is to surrender them, to hand them over to the Security Organ. It took me five days to give this statement. What I said at the time was at the end of the fifth day. And I don't understand what is not clear to you here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Everything is clear to me. But let's try to clarify this for the Trial Chamber. But it's absolutely clear to me. Tell me, has this been incorrectly translated too, when it say that is those documents were taken to the staff of the BH army, whose commander you were. That's not correct either?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Just a minute. You gave me a document which I had signed and which had a header. It was here a minute ago. There is a mistranslation here. There was no BH Army staff in Jablanica. There was a command there, and the 44th Mountain Brigade. There was no BH Army staff there. As an institution, it did not exist. Here there must have been a mistranslation when it says "staff." It was surrendered to the brigade command. It wouldn't be surrendered to me. If one unit found some documents, they're not going to hand documents over to some other command. They'll probably keep these documents for themselves. It doesn't say here that they were surrendered to the staff of the ABiH or to the command of the 44th Mountain Brigade. Sorry. I'm going a bit too fast. It say it was taken to the army staff, headquarters. That doesn't exist though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, is this incorrectly translated too, the last paragraph? You see before this list where it says that you personally made copies of these documents immediately. Has that been incorrectly translated?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the plural. Yes, I participated in that. When we handed those documents over -- yes, Zajko Sihirlic and I were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It says the 27th of July here, and it quite clearly states "I did that in order to be sure --"

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It should be the plural. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Here it's in the singular.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can only be in the plural.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's exactly the reason why -- one of the reasons why I wanted the Chamber to have the statements. Mr. Krsnik has jumped a paragraph there's an intervening paragraph. "Before we hand over the documents to the legal authorities of ABiH." Now, that's the direct examination that was sometime later. Now counsel is trying to say the copies were made "immediately." The document doesn't say anything about the copies being made immediately. It's a mischaracterisation of the statement and that's why I wanted the Chamber to have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We noticed that ourselves. You may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know what the English translation is like, but the Croatian version is absolutely clear. It's quite clear. This entire paragraph is quite clear in Croatian. We've -- our questions have been answered. I'm going to move on so as not to waste time. I have a lot of questions I want to ask about the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, after Zajko Sihirlic, who had the so-called diary after Zajko Sihirlic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Copies of that diary were made --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please. Will you answer the question. Who had it after --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will, but you won't let me answer. The diary was typed out. It was copied. It was given to the television so that they could make it public. We wanted as many people as possible to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You don't have to repeat that. You said that yesterday too.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've asked me many things that you asked me yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who was the next person to have the diary? Where was the manuscript located?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in a safe. Sihirlic the security officer had it in his brigade. That's what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When was the AID provided with the diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that they heard about it and then they came to ask you about it.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't a secret. The fact that we had it was not a secret. They were aware of the diary's existence, but they could have heard about its existence from anyone and everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The statement that you gave - and we will provide you with it now --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar show the witness the second statement that you gave on the 27th and on the 28th of June of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So that means you gave it a few months ago. On page 10 you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's the number of that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, here. [Interpretation] The number is D1/425.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters have a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: They have, the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page 10. Have you found it? It's the third paragraph. Can you see the third paragraph? And here you say -- the sentence starts with the words "In addition to that, the original of that diary was found by the Bosnian Army in Doljani." And now you say: "The Bosnian Army took over Doljani." And you don't say that they liberated it -- "in July 1993." And then you continue. "The diary was handed over to the security services of the Bosnian Army, which kept this diary until the end of the war." And you say that you then, in the year 1997 -- that "Zajko Sihirlic, the security officer from the BH Army and you handed this to the civilian authorities -- to the AID, handed this diary over to the authorities. And it wasn't at their request. You went there and hand the diary over to them." That's what it says in the statement. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was at their request.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's not what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, where does it say anything that suggests that they initiated contact with the AID? The English translation, at least- unless the B/C/S says something different - it says, "I think that it was in 1997 Mr. Sihirlic, a security officer of the BH Army and myself, hand it over to the authorities of BiH, AID." Now, if Mr. Krsnik can tell us what exactly it is that that sentence that's inconsistent with what the witness has said here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We've found this line in this paragraph. Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know what it says in the translation, but it -- the statement speaks for itself. And we've heard what the statement is. We'll draw our own conclusions. Could the Prosecutor not start interpreting this and arriving at conclusions. If it's inconsistent, you'll come to a conclusion. If it's consistent, you'll again come to your own conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, would you read in B/C/S the last sentence in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I think that it was in 1997 that Zajko Sihirlic, a BH Army security officer, and myself handed it over to the civilian authorities of the BiH, the AID."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
