utterances.text: Please tell me, who copied out the diary? Who copied out the diary from the manuscript?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been the typist or typists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who checked whether the printed copy of the document was a faithful reproduction of the original?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one checked this. They believed the typists. They had faith in the typists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When you have a look at a handwritten document -- at the handwritten document, can you confirm here in front of the Trial Chamber that this document was in chronological order?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To an extent. But certain periods were skipped. There were periods that were skipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could document -- could Exhibit P928C be provided now, please. 928C. Have a look at page 40, please. Have you found page 40?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What's the date?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please have a look at page 51 now. Could you tell us the date, please. Just a minute. For the sake of the transcript. What date is mentioned on page 51 and on page 40? Could you please repeat that for the sake of the transcript. What date can you see on page 40?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 51, this doesn't have anything to do with the diary, with the war diary, with what happened during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. For the sake of the transcript, Mr. Idrizovic, my question and the answer have not been recorded in the transcript. What date can you see on page 40? Could you have a look again. You have to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 40, the date is the 16th of November -- sorry, the 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The 16th of January, 1993. Now, please, can you just tell me, what date can you see on page 51?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date on page 51 is the 8th of November, 1986. But the text that -- it has nothing to do with the diary or with the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, don't be like that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Allow the witness to finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rados was a sportsman. He played handball. If you have a look at page 39, if you go back to page 39. Please, we're discussing. We are equal. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, we're not discussing. This is my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we're both discussing, so we have -- we're having a conversation here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, just finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1986, earlier on, on several pages in this diary he wrote out the schedules, the timetables for handball matches. He never did this in sequential order. It was not on each page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How do you know all of this?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, I can see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you write that diary?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Maybe you did. How do I know? Have a look at page 37. It says "handball." On page 38, there's nothing. On page 39, it says "handball." On page 40, "16th of January, 1993." And then again on page 51, "Handball." It was war. No one had much equipment down there. He had this diary, this notebook -- he probably used this notebook because it was small enough to fit in his pocket. So he must have found some old notebook. This is what I assume, because at the time no one had such materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please now open the diary on page 54. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What is the date written here?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 19 January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you put it on the ELMO, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Usher, can you please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It seems to me that I can see the date 19th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You do not see it well. Your eyesight seems to be bad here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No. Please open page 54. What is the date here, on 54?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 1993, very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, your microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you look at the document and unfortunately I suppose the Chamber doesn't have it in front of them, the document says what it says. We stipulate -- the Prosecution stipulate that is some of the entries are out of chronological order. Now, how is that an impeachment of this witness? He didn't say he wrote the document. This is how it is. So I don't understand how this is impeachment of the witness. There are parts of the document out of order, no dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, and why is then this witness here if we cannot verify the diary with him? Another thing that we have to establish here: The typed out version does not correspond with the blue-ink version, and we are going to come to that really very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please turn to page 55. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What is the date?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What date?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Just a moment, please. 19 January, 1993, Sunday. And 18 January 1993, it says "Monday." It was war, so the man must have forgotten what the date it was. It says "Sunday" and then "Monday." I didn't write the diary. It was Alojz who made the mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is that your assumption, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says here, "Monday."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sir, we have checked it in the computer. The 19th was Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't a clue which day or date it was. How would I know that, for Christ's sake?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please put it on the ELMO. The date, can you see it, the 18th of January, 1993? And now can we please turn to page 56. Can we have it on the ELMO. Page 56, what date do you see here?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it when it's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Look at it like this and then put it back on the ELMO, please. Can you see the date here?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the date. He does mention the date of 15th of April, 1997 [As interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please put it on the ELMO. Is it 1987 or 1989?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, it is indeed 1987. What does it say under that entry?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the date has something to do with the contents, with the text, but it has nothing to do with the diary. I can't see what it says here. I have to read the whole passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It says very clearly, "A meeting on the protection at work." That's day one. The second day the text continues, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wasn't paying attention to the text. But that is what I said a little while ago, that he was an athlete, that he played matches. He was also an official in the handball club of Jablanica. But this has nothing whatsoever to do with the text of the diary. This is a similar thing as the results of football -- of handball matches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you now please turn to page 60. What dates can you see here?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 17th and 18th January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did we not have these dates on page 54?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Alojz wrote. That's his problem, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You don't know what he wrote. Okay, then. Look at the page 61, please. What date can you see there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did we not have it on page 54?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously Alojz got mixed up on his dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well then. Can you please look at page 64 of the blue-ink version. What is the last word on that page? Can you please find the last word on page 64?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We are leaving around 4.00."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you now turn to page 65. What event is transcribed and what date can you see here?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, something about handball, something about sports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what is the date?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What has that got to do with anything? It has nothing whatsoever to do with the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please give me the date and the town that is mentioned. Does it not say "Treviso"?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 4th Congress," in abbreviation "Yugoslav and Italy in Treviso."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's move on. Can we have the usher showing you the typed-out version, 928D. Please open page 4 of this document. Can you please tell me, on page 4 what text follows the indication of 1400 hours? This seems to be a report of some sort.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am finding it very hard to read. My eyes get tired very quickly. Can you please tell me -- direct me towards the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. I will help you. Can you see the word "report." What text follows? How does that part of the text start?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to order number and in consultation with so and so."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, please take the so-called original of the diary.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Usher, can you please leave the blue-ink copy with the witness. We will need both.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I never said this was typed out correctly. Nobody checked and compared the two. But still I will have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please find in the diary 21st of January, 1993. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, we have it in the typed-out version and in the blue-ink copy. Can you tell me whether the wording is the same on the 21st of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little while ago we said that there was some confusion with the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm not referring to that. I'm talking about comparing what it reads in the blue-ink copy and in the typed-out copy.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not the same. But maybe under the same date the text is the same somewhere else, because there was some confusion with the dates. This same date may be appearing somewhere else, and that text Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 16355 to 16360. maybe can be found somewhere else. In the original, as you can see, one date appears in several places, so this may be the case here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I will help you. Open the page 142 of the blue-ink version, please. Is the text identical with the text in the typed-out document on page 4?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But all this text, all of these dates have nothing whatsoever to do with what we are talking about today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well, then. So the date 21st of January, 1993, in the typed-out version has nothing whatsoever to do with the text in the diary.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please then explain.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that January 1993 was when Alojz described their stay on the Ljubinka Mountain near Konjic. And for us this is absolutely irrelevant. It is not important for us from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it then typed out wrongly?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that was the case. In the same way Alojz made mistakes when he was writing his original, some mistakes were made when the diary was typed out. There is no way anybody could type out something without making mistakes. However, the typed-out version was only for our entertainment, to entertain us, for us to read and to amuse ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You used it to amuse yourself and the Prosecution used it as their official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1994, we used it for entertainment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think both of you are speaking at the same time, which is giving great difficulty to the interpreters. Witness, I understand that you're eager to give your evidence, give your testimony. And if you look at the screen, there will be English typed out on your screen. Whenever the typing is stopped, you may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't know whether this has been recorded. You said that the typed-out version was for your entertainment. But the Prosecution didn't use it for entertainment. They used it for translation. And I'm very glad that we were able to clarify that. We've seen a lot of things that do not match this in the two documents and we have been able to establish that together. Let's move on. Kindly tell us, please -- look at the page 146 of the blue-ink version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Krsnik, I may be stupid about this -- and you know, one of you will remind me -- yesterday when Mr. Scott was telling us what each exhibit represented -- and I thought he did it rather well, but obviously I'm confused now -- Exhibit 928 was called the English translation; 928A was the typed B/C/S diary; and then we had 928B, which was a photocopy of the blue-ink diary, if you like; and then C was the actual diary; and D was the copy of the typed B/C/S diary kept by the witness. Now, what I'm trying to find out -- and maybe this was said yesterday but I missed it: Was the translation which we have now -- maybe Mr. Scott would be better qualified -- was that the translation of the typed-up Jablanica version, or is it a translation of the blue-handwritten version?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Judge Clark, Your Honours, as best I can determine, since we did not have in our custody until a few days ago the blue-ink version, the English translation, which is 928, was based upon 928A. It's based on 928A. 928A, as Ms. Bos testified, was the version received by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 16th of March, 1998. And 928B was the copy of the handwritten diary first received by the OTP on the 10th of December, 1998. So it is correct, Your Honours. And what I just in fact -- just this one minute ago made a note to myself, any specific passages, any specific passages that the Prosecutor would seek to introduce into evidence or include in its brief would certainly be -- we will translate those directly from the blue-ink version. Again, we didn't have that until just a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have to clarify things. Your Honour, we have to make sure that things are clear to the very end. Thank you very much for your remark. Now I am confused. Your questions are so up to the point. There are two typed-out versions. One has been made by Mr. Idrizovic, or his colleagues; and the other version, the typed-out version, is one that we received through Ms. Bos. So they are both typed out versions, and the translation was made based on one or the other or both of them. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll say it again. The English translation, which is marked as 928, is, I believe, a translation of 928A, the copy of the typed document -- the typed B/C/S diary received by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 16th of March, 1998. That is where the translation comes from. The copy 928D, which is again, as counsel says, a typed B/C/S diary, is the copy that the witness brought with him to The Hague when he travelled here in connection with his testimony and which the witness testified on direct examination is the typed version that he has had continuously in his possession since 1993. So if the Chamber wants to compare, and if Mr. Krsnik wants to compare text between the typed versions, and if the suggestion is that sometime after AID received the typed version in 1997, that sometime after that the AID fabricated it, I suggest to the Chamber they can compare that against 928D, which is the copy of the typed diary that this witness has had in his possession continuously since 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, are they in different typewriters, or are they photocopies of the same thing? Are there any material differences in appearance?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Judge Clark, to give a -- to be completely, what I would consider, an authoritative answer to that, I would want to sit down and compare it myself. I believe they are documents -- I believe the text version, the typed versions are the same. But I say that -- please allow me to qualify that by not having compared it word for word myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I don't mean you to do that, but if we have to -- I don't mean for you to do that right now, but if we had Mr. Idrizovic's photocopy and the photocopy which you received, do they look similar? That's all I'm saying. Does the typeface look as if it's from the same typewriter? This is just a basic question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: They have that look.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It appears to be in what I would consider an italic font, the same point font, from -- the text -- the typing looks similar. Of course I can't comment on the B/C/S content. But the typing -- the format of the document looks similar. In 928D, which is signed by the witness on the front page, which he's said he's had with him, you will note that there are difference because at various times apparently -- for instance, on page 20, the witness has underlined some material for whatever particular interest to himself. So that's different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] My mike is not working. Thank you. Just as a very simple exercise, could we take page 2 of the typed version, which has a record number 00635504 in the book that you gave me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Some of the documents have been -- I have to admit, some of my copies have apparently been taken apart for different purposes and some -- I'm having a bit of trouble. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] What I was going to say is that that particular page that has that number, Prosecution number, appears to have quite a number of typographical errors. And just as a simple exercise, I picked that at random, could we compare that with the same page that we got from Mr. Idrizovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. It's just a question of having the time to make sure that we have both the same pages. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Clark, when you look at Mr. Idrizovic's version and the one that we got from the Prosecution, you will immediately see that there is a difference. The dates have been crossed out in the Prosecutor's version, whereas in Mr. Idrizovic's version they can still be seen. The majority of dates have been blackened out in the text on the copy that we received from the Prosecution. And in the typed-out version that we have from Mr. Idrizovic, they are visible. However, Mr. Idrizovic is here. He can assist us. And yesterday he said that several typewriters were used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was typed in several occasions, probably using several typewriters. But I believe that this particular text was typed on one typewriter, but I have to have a close look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We typed it wherever we had the time and the possibility to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I suggest in light of the questions that have been raised, and particularly by Judge Clark, which as always are highly pertinent and helpful, could we possibly take a moment's break and make copies of those corresponding pages so everyone will have them in front of them at the same time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I find and them -- superficially, that's all one can say -- the exact typographical errors appear on both pages. And that's a page I picked at random.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have them too now, Your Honour. So if you're satisfied, perhaps we don't need further copies. But the same appears to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I might do another exercise later to see if I can find another random one, just to satisfy myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We left off with the 24th of January, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Have you found that in the blue-ink version? Can you please read the beginnings of the first eight lines if you can.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the eight lines? You want me to read all the eight lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: They're short. If you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just asking whether I should do that. "They are digging themselves in as moles."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. My mistake. Are you reading on the 24th or the 23rd? Please read on the 24th January 1993. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Shelling, shooting during the night around the HVO headquarters -- the Ovnovic wedding party." Do you want me to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the hotel, the military police dragged out of their rooms all the Croat drivers from the vicinity of Tuzla and they beat them up in the parking lot in front of the hotel. A. Han--" That is probably Aleksin Han. I can't really read it that well. What it says here, "this has been conveyed to the commander of our military police about the people from Tuzla who have been beaten up."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please read on.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The prevention of an onslaught from Risovac and Doljani. All the hunters' houses are full."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay, then. Line 6, I believe that you've seen it. It says something -- just for the record, you are reading from the document that we call P928C. In line 6 it says something like "Allah-u-ekber." Have you found it in this document that you're holding in your hand, document P928C?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't found it. It says "A. Han," that stands for Aleksin Han, that is the bridge from the municipality in the direction of Mostar. But I can't discern what it says here. I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you put it on the ELMO. Maybe I'll be able to decipher what it says. Turn it around, please. Can you please show me the date, the 24th of January. Line 6, can you see it? It says very clearly "Allah-u-ekber." That is not Aleksin Han. That is "Allah-u-ekber." It reads very well "Allah-u-ekber."

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is the abbreviation for Aleksin Han and the rest of it I can't read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. Then. In the typed-out version page 5, is there any text after "Livaja"?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably even the typist who was typing this out wasn't able to read it, just like I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But is there any text further on? Not just "Allah-u-ekber," but is there any text, and sit identical? Can you take a look?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no text after that. What do you want me to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm just drawing a conclusion. I don't want you to say anything.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite clear. It "A. Han" here and then "in" and then I can't read the following word.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We can carry on. But it quite clearly says "ekber," E-K-B-E-R, and this is quite clear, it says "Allah." And you said that you knew his handwriting. How is it that you can't read it now?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't. I know his handwriting. I can read the following 1.000 words and I probably won't have to skip a single word. I'll probably have to read them all out. But I can't read -- I can't read this word.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on. Have a look at page 186, in document P928C the date, 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, 186. The date is the 15th of April, 1993. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The date is the 15th of April. Have you found the date?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Have a look at page 188 now. What's the date on this page, on page 188?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That carries the date from the previous page. It has the same date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's have a look at page 189 now.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What's the date on this page?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something between the 16th and the 17th. He probably wrote down the 17th and then corrected it and put down the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So these corrections are clear, the corrections he made to the date.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you know he made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it assume. He probably did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, have a look at page 191. Has the date been corrected here?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the same. He probably mixed up the dates and then corrected them later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: He did that or someone else?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why someone else would do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Could you now have a look at that handwritten version. Close the diary. Have a look at the first page, the first page, where it sort of starts. And in the left-hand corner, is there something handwritten, a name that is handwritten?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says "Rados Alojz."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please put it on the ELMO so we can all see it clearly. Is that his signature?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it occurs quite often in the documents. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, so you're claiming under oath that this is Rados Alojz's signature?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whose signature would it be?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm putting the question to you.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course it is. You can see this quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could you please provide the witness with document P68.4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krsnik, when you provide the references -- when you provide the references for a document, you aren't close enough to the microphone, and it's difficult for the interpreters to hear you then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. You know, I get a bit carried away. This is the document that was used yesterday. It's the first page. And it's the document that was provided by the Prosecutor. [Previous translation continues] ... both signatures putting together. [Interpretation] So this one that has been circled. And can you put the signature close to the one on the notebook. [In English] Close to this signature. [Interpretation] Can you put the one under the other. [In English] One under another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're all laymen here. We aren't experts. Yesterday you said that the signature that has been encircled -- well, can you tell us now to us laymen, are these signatures identical?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one was signed in 1987 and the other in 1990. I apologise. This one was in 1986 and this one in is 1990, so that's a four-year difference. Are you sure? Do you know how you signed your name four years ago? But the handwriting is obviously the same, but it was probably signed at a different speed. But in any case, we're not experts. We're not graphologists. There are people who can establish what the case is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But, sir, you claim that this is Alojz Rados's signature. That's what you categorically stated yesterday.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've seen Rados Alojz's signature thousands of time, when I worked with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. You see, this says quite -- absolutely identical. And have a look at the letter "A." You can see how -- you can see that they are identical.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's put this into a different perspective.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, let's move on. We've got another signature in this so-called diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the document P428.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what's the number of that document? Would you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P428.1. It's the document that was used yesterday by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is that 424.1?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, 428. 428.1. But maybe we've made a mistake, because my colleague and I, we worked until very late last night. Maybe it is 424. [In English] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you. Madam, this signature, put close to these three -- these two. Can we show the -- oh, yes, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, we're all laymen here, and we're looking at three signatures. Do you still claim that they are all identical?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on, then. Let's go back to 928C. Have a look at page 115, Mr. Idrizovic, please. Page 115. Could you put it on the ELMO, please. You can see what it says in black. Do you claim this to be Rados's handwriting? Would you make such a claim under oath?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is written in capital letters. I don't know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I am asking you: Is this Alojz Rados's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't appear to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please have a look at page 114. And thank you. It's the same document. It's in the same document, 928C. Is that Alojz Rados's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, this handwriting, it's all in capital letters. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm asking you, is this Alojz Rados's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not very familiar with his handwriting when the text is written in capital letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And have a look at document -- at Exhibit 68.6. They are capital letters too -- correction, 68.4. 68.4. And the printed part, is that Alojz Rados's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the diary that he had in the company for years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you can recognise this handwriting that is in capitals.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was his diary. It can only be his handwriting. It couldn't be anyone else's handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's your conclusion then, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what would you conclude from that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, look, half of that document is in capital letters. Let's have a look at page 131.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I haven't been called here as an expert, as a graphologist. My sight is very bad, and I wanted to ask you whether I could rest my eyes for a bit. The gentleman here can't treat me as if it were a graphologist. So please, this should be a task for the experts. I shouldn't be turned into something that I'm not or treated as something that I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you made very categorical claims and you recognised this. That's why I'm putting these questions to you now. Have a look at page 131.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already answered your question. I really can't read the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I know your point. And if you draw attention to certain pages, that's enough. There's no need to identify every single place in that diary at all. And I think, you know, we have been going on on this kind of testimony for quite a long time and everybody is tired. We only have less than ten minutes to go for the morning session. Could we break here and continue at 2.30 this afternoon so that everybody will have a rest, especially the witness will rest his eyes. Thank you very much. We'll resume at 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.49 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we have received your motion objecting the admission of the Rados diary, and I think the Bench has been informed about your position concerning with the admission of the Rados diary. So Mr. Krsnik, it is our intention to have this witness go back home today, because this is the last day of this week, and the witness has been in The Hague for over a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours. But the position to clarify certain issues regarding my positions with the witness. My position may be such and such, but we have to clarify this matter with the witness. And obviously he will go home today. I see no reason for him to stay on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. You may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, I'll try and be brief, so please be so kind as to reply very briefly. Do you know why in the copy of the manuscript, you know, the typed copy, do you know why the text is not complete? Do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. But I think that for this Trial Chamber and for the whole case, this typed part, this typed document is not important. I think I made a mistake in providing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, please, if you know about this: Who decided what would be copied and what would be omitted in the typed text?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one made such decisions. A copy of the diary was given to the typist, for the typist to type out. What the typist managed to read, the typist typed out. And obviously if typist was unable to read certain parts, the typist skipped that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And who decided what should be added to that text? Who decided what should be -- who decided to add things that are not contained in the original?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I've not seen counsel put forward any evidence of thing that is have been added. That's a complete mischaracterisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, would you please make it clear for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I thought that it was clear. And when I hear such objections, start panicking, because after two or three hours of cross-examination it still doesn't seem to be clear what was added and what was omitted. If necessary, however, I will provide another piece of evidence very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not been recorded in the transcript correctly. I asked who decided that the text -- that certain sentences would be added to the text that weren't in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know the answer to this question? Who decided about this, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My objection is the same, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krsnik, you said that you'd show an example to us on this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness first answer, and then I will show an example. I asked him whether he had any knowledge of this. What's in dispute here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's completely a misleading way to the witness to put that question -- to suggest to the witness, to put a suggestive question to the witness which is not based on evidence in the record and then have the witness try to guess at a response. If there's a specific example, which I submit respectfully there has not been today so far -- if counsel wants to take the witness to something that he sees and says "this is added," so that we all know what he's talking about. Judge Clark does, Judge Diarra does, Mr. President, you do, and I do, then we can look at that and the witness can say whether it's been added or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, so far as I know certain parts were redacted - redacted - concerning the -- concerning with the time maybe in the typed version. Do you mean that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I was very clear, and I have already shown this. Parts of the text were omitted, parts of the text that were in the so-called original. These parts are not contained in the typed version of the text. I don't know. Perhaps the Prosecutor and I are sitting in two different courtrooms. But I will now show, and I thought I had already shown you this -- but it's easy to check this in the transcript. I'll provide you with another example. There are many such examples. I'll provide you with an example in which text was added. This was something that is not contained anywhere. There are sentences which are added that have been changed and that aren't contained in the original. So I think my question was quite clear. We'll find it out. The page, I think, is the following: [In English] Exhibit P928D and 928C. First give it -- give 928C.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you please go to page 203. I won't bother you any more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I understand Mr. Krsnik. He's doing a difficult job, and he's clinging to whatever he can. That's normal. But the typed version has nothing to do with the subject that we are discussing here. It has absolutely nothing to do with it. We have the original here, and there is a photocopy of the original. He's asking me about things that are totally irrelevant and things I know nothing about. If you give something to be typed out -- well, none of us had the time to -- in the course of the war when we were in difficulties, we didn't have the time to read out to see whether something had been typed out correctly or not. That was not important. That's not important. I can answer Mr. Krsnik's questions, but I think that he is wasting time without reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Since you said that this original has nothing to do with the typed version, I will not ask you any other questions.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. I said that it was possible that the girls who were typing it out made a mistake. I never compared the two texts, and I don't know whether someone else did that. Are you content with that answer now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, we'll decide what is relevant and what is not. Please do as the Defence counsel requests you to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's clear. I'm waiting for the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at the text. I don't want to tire you too much, you know. Do you have page 203 in front of you, where it says, "Thursday, the 22nd of April, 1993." Could you have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 203? The date -- I can't see a date. I'm sorry, yes, the 22nd of April. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please. Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you have a look at the first three sentences. Could you read them out. They're not very long.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I slept and even had a bath and shaved at Marinko's. His wife was there and child."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. And now, could you please read out on page 18 -- could you read out the typed part, under the date the 22nd of April, 1993. Page 18. It's under the date the 22nd of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I even shaved at Marinko's. His brother and parents were there too."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And then? Can you continue.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I felt a little better, relieved. It was a nice day."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, who added this? If you know, of course.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, thanks very much. I have many such examples, as many as you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, should I provide other examples? We have a list of such examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Have a look at page 143 [As interpreted] -- page 142 in the blue-ink copy.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So we are looking at 142.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Have you found it? How does that page begin? With what words?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The list for Ljubina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many people are listed on this page. Just give us their number. How many of them?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People may not be following what we are talking about. There are numbers here, but some people have been crossed out from the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What is their total number, the number of these people?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten -- I'm sorry, nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please put the page on the ELMO. As far as I can see, the last number is 11, and only one name has been crossed out.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Under "6" and under"8" two people have been crossed out or blurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you now look at the typed-out version, page 5. "The internal remark," it says here. "Try and secure another communications station with Kolibe." Where does that say under number "1", sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to take time to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm putting it to you after the list for Ljubina, on that same page, that sentence is missing. And later on where does it say in the diary the commander and then the assistant cook? Where does that say on the blue-ink copy?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No. I'm referring to page 142. Where does it say "the commander --" I'm referring to this list for Ljubina. Where does it say "commander" and where does it say "the assistant cook"?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. It doesn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Exactly. And how come that this text on 142 says [B/S/C spoken], and does that exist on page 5?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will have to ask Alojz why he didn't write that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, don't tell me that. We're comparing the blueprint copy with the typed-out copy. Let's leave Alojz alone. Does that exist in the blue-ink copy?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the list of the same people, but the typist did not want to copy the same list again to avoid repetition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sir, there is a name and there is a place to it. This is what it doesn't exist in the typed-out version, but it has been added "the Commander and the assistant cook," which is not to be found in the blue-ink copy.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What has that got to do with anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher's assistance. Can you please give Madam Registrar the document D1/434, and can you please distribute it among the Bench and others in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday you said to my learned friend that you handed documents over to "our people from the AID." Who is it who you consider "our people"? What did you mean by "our people from the AID"?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mean anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me please: What is the AID and what is its function?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's beyond the scope, and it's not the purpose of this witness to come and testify about AID. It was to come and testify about the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. I think the AID issue has come up for many, many times. Let's drop it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a very relevant part of the whole story, because the AID is involved in the entire story. But let me now reply to my learned friend, but may the witness be excused for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you have a particular question, so ask your question directly to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But of course. That is exactly what I wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. That is not. Your question is: What is the AID and what is its function? Which is far away from the subject matter of this rebuttal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that you handed the diary over to the AID in 1997; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now put the question to the witness who is or what is AID?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same thing as the SIS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have the same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We understand that. Well, Mr. Krsnik, if you claim that AID changed or made that diary, you just put your case to this witness and ask a direct question to this witness to see whether the witness knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, this is what I have been asked to do. Let's make our lives easier and let me put it to you. As in the criminal charges and request for investigation against Bakir Alispahic, the director of the AID, who was -- who performed that duty between 1992 and 1996, if Irfan Ljevakovic, his deputy; and Enver Mujezinovic, his deputy; the AID --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well -- yes, please finish your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm putting it to you, sir, that as it says here, they were involved in the forgery of identification cards, various activities, political assassinations, cooperation with Iranian secret services and al Qaeda and that this diary has also been used for propaganda purposes and that you participated in that. Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now you have gone over the top, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is the same thing. It's a speech. It's argument. That's all it is. If he's putting the issue, as you, Mr. President, invited him to you, would be to put -- to put, "I put it to you, sir, that the diary we've been talking about is nothing more than a fabrication." Is that true? That's putting the question, not giving speeches about AID, about talking about a case that none of us know anything else about and is not relevant to this courtroom. He can put the specific relevance question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krsnik, you may direct our attention to that document. That document 434 and let us see where this document mentioned that Rados diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document there's no specific mention of the diary, in this particular document, but what is mentioned is an investigation that is being carried out because these people have forged documents. And if the AID kept the diary since 1997 and only handed it over this year, then I believe that I may put the questions to the witness to go for the credibility of the document and of the whole situation. These people have been in prison for some time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately they have been released from prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you mean that you based all your allegations on speculation? Well, well, those people forged documents; maybe it's true and maybe it's not. But how do you arrive at the conclusion that this diary is also forged by AID? You may put this question to the witness to see if the witness knows or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have, Your Honour, but then Mr. Scott intervened. Then the gentleman told me that I am exaggerating. I'm trying to have a conversation with the witness. This diary was in the possession of the AID. It is a fact that has been established. If that fact hasn't been established, I will move on. How come you will not allow me to establish the origin of this diary and his whereabouts for such a long number of years. This is just -- this document that I'm presenting to you now is a fact, a factual document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, from a very brief glance at this document - and it's not easy to digest - just scanning it for milliseconds, I see that the venue of the alleged offences, if they have anything whatever to do with the Rados diary, I doubt, is in the FBiH. Our case is dealing with Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993. The Federation came into existence a long time afterwards. Your argument is about as valid as saying, because some policemen have been prosecuted successfully in California for beating up suspects, that any investigation by police in Oregon is invalid. They just -- it's not logical what you're saying. It doesn't follow. What Judge Liu is asking you to do is while we have this witness here, who's a key witness in relation to the diary, to put to him what your case is. And surely you've got something to put to him that's a little better than some bad eggs, possibly, might be prosecuted in Sarajevo for activity which occurred subsequent to the events in this case. Surely you've got something more than that to put to this person, to say what your case is in relation to the diary. We've got this blue-ink diary, as you call it, and you've got that in front of you. Now, what is your case in relation to that diary? Whatever about the errors that were made in the typing in 1993. What is your case? Are you going to say that you are going to call evidence that AID forged this diary, or are you saying because some of them are being prosecuted for illegal activity in 2002, that they therefore must have forged the diary in 1993? That's what it sounds like to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Clark, again you make me panic. I thought everything was clear. And now what am I to do? Obviously this is exactly what I was going to say. It is absolutely clear that more than one person has been involved, more than one handwriting is visible. There's no visible chronological order. Things relevant to 1991, 1993 are mixed up. The signature is dubious. And I believe that my case is clear, and this is what I am trying to prove in my cross-examination. What I'm saying is that people were adding things because they had the time to do that and not abandon this is something that they used for entertainment. People typed out whatever they wanted and however they wanted, and this is something that we have been dealing with for so long here. And it was nothing but entertainment to them. And finally, my learned friend has been telling a story about the AID for over a year. Let us see who this AID is. Its key person was detained in 2002, but he didn't commit the crimes in 2002. He was committing crimes prior to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We've gone round and round and round this issue for 14 months, and we have said you're not to give evidence, and I think you know that. You have made accusations about AID on dozens of occasions, but you haven't called a single primary source witness to help us on this. You've just made wild accusations. You know the difference between calling a primary source witness and making accusations in court. Now, if you have a specific case about this diary that, it wasn't found in Doljani that, it wasn't -- that it was in the hands of someone else, that there were several diaries going round, then put it to this witness because he's the appropriate person to deal with it, if you're criticising aspects of the diary and saying there's different handwriting, you've done that extremely well and we've taken that point. But you must now instead of making wild accusations put your case. Well, you don't have to, but you fail to do so at your peril.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And by the way, Mr. Krsnik, we all agree that this diary was in the possession of the AID for quite a while. There is no dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Clark, you know very well that we discussed the thing during an ex parte hearing and that we did have a person here, and I told you during that first ex parte session. And at the second ex parte session I explained all the other reasons that I have. But I don't want to belabour upon that now. We can come back to that later maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I'm putting it to you Zajko Sihirlic was your assistant but not in the brigade. The security officer in the brigade myself Mustafa Skampo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You are absolutely misinformed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is Zajko Sihirlic a secret agent of the AID?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will have to ask somebody in the AID that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You adhered to the thesis that it was Zajko Sihirlic who took the diary from the headquarters in Doljani.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who was the first person who put his hands on the diary? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police took all the documents from Doljani and handed them over to Sihirlic as the officer in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did not the entire furniture -- wasn't the entire furniture brought in front of your headquarters and you and Sihirlic were the ones who found the documents in that furniture and you and him were the first to put your hands on those alleged documents?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry that you are so badly informed. I haven't completed my answer, sir. My headquarters was in the administrative building of the hydroelectrical powerplant, and nothing ever entered my premises, the premises where my office was. Nothing the size of a match or bigger, nothing from Doljani or elsewhere. Mr. Krsnik, I am an honest and honourable person, and never ever did I allow anything stolen from anybody to enter either my house or my workplace. And please bear that in mind in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who was it who planned the operation in Doljani? Are you going to tell us that you did not participate in that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely didn't participate in that. The operation was planned by the command of the 44th Mountain Brigade, and I was never a member of that command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you their superior?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Are you asking me to go over the same ground again and again? I believe that your time is rather restricted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, I'm not going to ask you to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [In English] D1/419.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the version you gave to the investigators, you said that Doljani was liberated by the BH Army. Who was it liberated from? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you. But first you tell me who was Doljani liberated from by the HVO before that. Can you tell me that? Because that's how things happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Kindly tell me. I have a report in front of you that was compiled for the purposes of this Office of the Prosecutor in Doljani. There was an atrocious crime which took place on the day when you liberated it. 35 civilians were massacred and 250 women and children were taken to the camp in Jablanica. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a crime was committed, then criminals should be taken to task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were 250 Croatian women and children taken to the camp in Jablanica which was under your control?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The camp in Jablanica was never under my control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And were the women and children taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this has nothing to do with me. And can you please disallow these questions, because I didn't organise, I didn't plan, I didn't carry out the operation, and I wasn't in charge of any of the camps. And can you please ask the counsel not to remind me of those times and not to tell lies. I explained very clearly what my position was at the time, and I believe that the counsel is wasting time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, are these questions related to the Rados diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Credibility and the Rados diary. The Rados diary was just something that was supposed to avert our eyes from what really happened on that day. On that day Doljani was liberated, yes, but from the civilians of the Croatian ethnicity. And these were children and women who were taken to the camp where they spent another year. And the witness knows it, and that's why I am putting this question to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, that may be true, Mr. Krsnik, but that is not the subject matter of this proceeding. You have to bear in mind about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am bearing that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, sir: Are you aware that an investigation in being carried against you both in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and according to some witnesses, also an investigation is being carried out against you by this Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, but I'm not afraid of appearing in front of any court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Have you negotiated with the Prosecutor's Office along these lines or about your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You understand my question.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you at all. I really don't know what you're saying. If Idrizovic should be held responsible for a crime, then everyone in the former Yugoslavia would be a criminal then. Please don't say such things. There's no sense. Don't make me be impolite. Really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm not attributing anything to you, sir. But the report against people for whom there is reasonable suspicion of having committed crimes, in this report, you are number 5. Cipo Safet [phoen] is the first one, Maris Muhamed the second, Omer Mirsad, Subara Resic [phoen], Idrizovic Safet, Kovacevic Enis, Sihirlic Zajko, the person we have been speaking about, Zebic Emin, and Kuric Said [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I just want to be clear. Is counsel basing all these allegations on Exhibit D1/419? Is that what all this is being based on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We also want to be guided, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also have Exhibit D1/428. It's a report against the same gentleman submitted by the SIS. That's the Croatian part, the counterpart of the AID. And it's against the same gentleman, and it mentions proceedings, criminal proceedings, that were instituted or that were to be instituted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are we furnished with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we provide the Exhibit D1/428. Unfortunately it hasn't been translated, but I would like to distribute it to you. These are document that is I have received from the Prosecution, and they all bear a Prosecution number. Yes. For the sake of the transcript, it's D1/428.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday you told the Prosecution that you weren't in Grabovica when an atrocious crime was also committed by the BH Army; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how would I be there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, look, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, your commander, in a letter and in an investigation -- I have a court report. This was provided to me by the Prosecution. He say that is you were at the meeting. I will read out this part and tell you where, and I'll give the document to the Court. It's Exhibit number D1/421?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please distribute it. I have an English version and a B/C/S version too. And D1/422. It's a statement made by Sefer Halilovic to the investigating judge in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've now been directed to four or five different documents. Could we possibly do one document and question at a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think we have already finished the document D1/419. Am I right, Mr. Krsnik? Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. And then Exhibit D1/421, the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Have a look at page 5, please. In his statement, Sefer Halilovic, who sent to Alija Izetbegovic, the President, and his -- in his statement which he gave to the investigating judge with regard to the crimes committed by the BH Army in Grabovica, he said, "In order to make preparations for the main axis of attack where Z. Suljevic was also present, V. Kric, Safet Idrizovic, Enis Kovacevic, Safet Indic, he says you've got the green light from the president for the above-mentioned operation in order to help Mostar, and I'm placing various things at your disposal, et cetera." Were you at that meeting in which preparations were being made for an attack against Grabovica, where an atrocious crime was committed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. An atrocious crime was committed in Grabovica, and that is a disgrace for the BH Army. It was a disgraceful act on the part of the BH Army at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What about Doljani?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just a minute. I haven't finished. You've put several questions to me. I think that the entire Grabovica case was here in front of the Prosecution. One should know who was responsible for what was done there. I know from the press that this case was referred back to the local authorities, to the local judiciary, and as a man, as a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I'm very disappointed to see that the prosecution in the judicial system in Bosnia and Herzegovina was not in a position, didn't want to deal with that case, solve that case. As far as I can tell from the press, on the basis of what I have read in the press, this case has been referred back to the Prosecution here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question was --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. Just a minute. No units from Jablanica - and I know this for a fact - no single man from Jablanica participated in that crime. The identity of the persons who participated in the crime is very well known. And just one other thing: When representatives of the high command go to their subordinates, then obviously a meeting is held. I and no one from Jablanica was with Sefer at a meeting of any kind. We didn't participate in a meeting at which the action in 1993 against Mostar was planned, because our units didn't plan that action and they didn't participate in that action either. And I think it is high time for this noise to do with the army to be taken away from Jablanica, to be removed from Jablanica. As far as Doljani is concerned, an action was undertaken. I think that any military action is a legitimate action if no crimes are committed. If there were crimes in Doljani, the perpetrators should be held accountable. That's no problem at all. And I personally won't feel sorry for anyone if that person committed a crime, that person should be held accountable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You haven't answered my question. Were women and children taken to the camp in Jablanica -- to the museum?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken to the camp -- they were taken to the museum. They were accommodated in the museum. All civilians, all Muslims from Capljina and Stolac who were expelled were placed in that museum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what did children of two or three years of age and what did the women do there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they did there. I never went to that facility. All I know is that my wife took food to the family of a colleague of hers very often, and that family is very grateful to me for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go into private session so that I can put a question to this witness. I want to protect someone's identity. I don't want it to be made public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But Mr. Krsnik, I have to remind you that -- the time. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the museum is concerned, the task of the unit which was under my command was only to provide external security for buildings, because it's a big building and the Red Cross had its warehouse in that building. And I haven't finished yet. I've got other things to add. There were exhibits from the museum there. There were many weapons which were there as trophies and there was other equipment. The library was there. Many other things too. The task of the unit that was under my command in that part was to protect that part of the museum. But they were forbidden to have anything to do with the people who were there, whether these were Muslim civilians or Croatian civilians or Croatian soldiers. Their sole task was to provide security for the building, for the part of the building that was not used for the purposes that you have been referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know Marinko Ljoljo.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Marinko very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The statement that he gave to investigators of the Prosecution, in that statement he accuses you that on the 15th of April, 1993, you personally arrested him and sent him to the Jablanica camp. This is Exhibit D1/427.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have it distributed. It's in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you do that or did you not do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm going to ask that we wait until all of us know what the document says. You can't ask the question and in the meantime be handing out the material, Mr. President. I object to that procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, do you have any more documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a pile of documents, but I'm trying to get through them as quickly as possible in accordance with the promise I made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you have more documents, would you please furnish us right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
