utterances.text: I would also like to show you -- were you authorised by Arif Pasalic to arrest anyone you wanted to -- or rather, to arrest anyone who was suspicious in the territory of the municipality of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President. I'm sorry. I know counsel feels rushed. I understand that. I've been rushed before myself. But we can't just put ten exhibits -- we can't simply table ten exhibits and put ten different questions and jump from item to item to item. I would like to be able to follow the question and answers. I would like to be able to follow the parts of the documents which counsel is putting to the witness to see if they're being put correctly. He cannot simply -- it's not fair to the witness, and in respect, it's not fair to me or to the Chamber. One document, one question at a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, where are we? Are we still at document 427, or we've finished it already?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've been waiting for an answer. I asked him a question which regarded this document, and it's a document in which this is quite clearly stated, Mr. Marinko Ljoljo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I ask that the question be re-put, Mr. President. If counsel could direct us to the part of the statement he's referring to, since it's several -- since it's a nine or ten-page statement or something, we -- can we please be shown where this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the first page, 00355469. That's the Prosecution number. It's on the first page, the first major paragraph, the last three sentences in the first paragraph. [In English] ... "asked him what was going to happen to us. He answered that we would be handed over to the military police, and that is what happened."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The question -- again, Mr. President, the question that was put at line -- that's my point. On page 90, line 4 -- we're about to lose it is -- were you authored by Arif Pasalic to arrest anyone you wanted to? That was the last question put to this witness a few moments ago I have no idea how that relates to the statement we've been directed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's another document. D1/423. That's the number of the document that the Prosecutor is referring to now. And I'm going to distribute it now. But please can you answer my first question about Marinko Ljoljo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, have you finished using the document 427?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the witness hasn't answered my question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't get a word in. Can't you see?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one time Marinko Ljoljo worked together with me in the school. I know him very well. On the 15th of April, when Jablanica was shelled for the first time, and when we had the first victims in Jablanica -- and I'm going to have to expand on this with a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please don't, then.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then I won't answer. I have to answer this at length. It's not the former command of the HVO which was left on the 2nd of April of that year was across the road from my command. We were neighbours. And for a certain period of time, when things were good -- please. Please. Now you want to tell me that I arrested Marinko Ljoljo and that I put him in prison. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Marinko Ljoljo says. That's not me.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Marinko Ljoljo has the right to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I object to this. I've done it repeatedly now. That is not what the statement says. It does not say that. And I ask again, Mr. President, one statement and one question at a time. And that's why the Chamber should have these statements. It does not say what Mr. Krsnik says it says. I object to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I've read it. That's true. It's only after he was arrested on somebody else's orders that he decided that as he knew Mr. Idrizovic, that he'd speak to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think you read two sentences of this statement. Just ask a simple question: Is that true in that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I didn't want to read everything out. If you read it from the beginning to the end, it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But is this correct or not? That's the first question. And which was the army, and under whose command was it? Who threatened them and said that if they didn't surrender they would shoot? Who was in command of that army?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true to say that he was arrested. I started answering, but I wasn't allowed to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So it's not true. Very well. Let's turn to D1/423. I only have the Croatian version. But it's a very short text. It's a question I want to ask you. There's only one sentence. Did you receive authorisation from Arif Pasalic, the commander of the 4th Corps, to bring in all suspicious persons from the territory of those two municipalities? An authorisation was given to your counterpart in Konjic, Catic Mirsad, and to you in Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never received such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we distribute D1/423.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, is this Arif Pasalic's signature?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Arif's -- Arif Pasalic's signature. But this has nothing to do with the relationship between the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council, and the BH Army. This was an internal affair, and it concerned the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. But did you receive that authorisation to bring people in?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did. To bring in the commander of the military police, of our military police. I was authorised to bring him in. But this is -- this was in November 1992, and at the time there was no conflict between the BH Army and the HVO. So please don't refer to this. This has nothing to do with what we are discussing. You are using the wrong documents. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Could we have help from the translation booth so the rest of us can even know what the document is about since counsel has not provided a translation. Could someone just read this document to the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krsnik, would you please read that document to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you put it on the ELMO, please -- but I'll read it out. "Republic of BiH, the Army of BiH Republic, 4th Corps Command. Authorisation. I hereby authorise the commander of the OSO Konjic, Mirsad Catic, and of the OSO in Jablanica, Safet Idrizovic, to bring in all suspicious persons from the territory of these two municipalities. And this is in connection with the proceedings which are being conducted in Parsovici. And I ask them to do this through their organs. Commander Arif Pasalic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It doesn't have any date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I ask Mr. Krsnik something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, witness, I think we have passed this section. Let us move on. We really want you to go back home today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the last -- or rather, the penultimate document -- and we will finish very soon now: D1/426. It consists of only one sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And it reads as follows: The Herceg Stjepan Brigade, 3rd Battalion, Mijat Tomic, Doljani, Jablanica. To Stipo Polo personally, the commander, handwritten. From Mostar, the 4th of May, 1993, at 2200 hours. Release all arrested civilians in Doljani and Sovici. Continue detaining military men who are fit to do their military service. The chief of the HVO main staff, Milivoj Petkovic." Did you provide this document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the last document, D1/433. And first of all, here is my question: In Slobodna Bosna in a newspaper in Sarajevo, did you react to an article? Did you send a letter to this newspaper reacting to an article? You have the text in front of you. It's the second column and it's the fourth paragraph. You explain why you react, and you say, "I'm also reacting because you put the text under the heading 'Hark,' which makes the readers think that the people who defended and managed to defend Jablanica from the Ustasha were really for The Hague." A minute ago you said that you thought that all perpetrators of crimes should be prosecuted. But here you're saying that no crimes were committed anywhere. So who are the Ustasha then, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a long time the present Bosnia and Herzegovina, both in the predominantly Croatian areas as well as in the predominantly Muslim areas, the press carried the thesis that people in Jablanica were guilty of the crimes in Srebrenica, for the crime in Uzdol, for the crime in Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Trusina.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and so on and so forth. I'm speaking about Jablanica. I'm not going to talk about the municipality of Konjic. And then in Slobodna Bosna, in the free Bosnia an interview appeared with Mirko Zelenika, who put my name in a very ugly context. So this was my angry reaction to his ugly words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll be very brief. If I can have the usher's assistance, please, to hand out four documents which we'll look at very quickly to the Defence counsel and to the Judges, please. I'll come to those momentarily, Mr. President. And I can assure the Chamber -- there's only about one or two lines in each one that I will just simply direct the witness's attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, directing your attention to some of the units -- the names of some of the units that came to the Jablanica area at different times in 1993, is it correct that the so-called "Zuka's Unit" was from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, the first time I saw them was on Igman, which is a mountain above Sarajevo. I don't know if they were in Sarajevo itself, but they were on Mount Igman, very close to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the interests of time, I'm going to mention three other units to you. The Black Swans, the Silver Fox, the Igman's Wolves. Were those all units from outside the Jablanica area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only Black Swans were never in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you, sir, a member -- ever a member of any of those either Zuka's Unit, Black Swans, Silver Fox, or Igman's Wolves? Were you ever a member of those units?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were here very often in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, my question, sir, was: Were you a member of those units, any of those units?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever have any command responsibility concerning either -- or any of those four units?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to look at documents -- just so you'll know what I'm referring torque I'll have to ask the translators to assist, since these documents have only become relevant since lunchtime today. 611, you have that, sir. And if I could ask the -- direct the courtroom's attention to the second page, toward the bottom of the page, item A. Sir, I'm simply going to read a line to you. I'll ask for translation to assist us. And then if you -- then I'll ask you a question if that's true. Sir, this is a report from ECMM for the 27th of September, 1993. Now, on the second page of that report, it says: "There were 640 Croats in Jablanica which included 200 from Doljani who were living in the museum in the town. They were not being treated badly by the Muslims but conditions were very bad in the museum." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. However, let me tell you that the conditions of life in Jablanica, generally speaking, were rather bad. My family, as well as all the other families, spent the entire year in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention, sir -- we're trying to move very quickly. Forgive me. Direct your attention, please, to Exhibit 640.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, to page 3 of that report, item D.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Team M-1 Jablanica visited a refugee camp located in the museum of the town. It houses some 400 Muslims and 300 Croats. Some of the latter from Konjic was apparently promised transport to Medjugorje but have since been interned. The conditions in the camp are extremely poor. So were the conditions of the camp extremely poor for both for the 300 Croats and the 400 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Exhibit 664.01, an ECMM report for the 5th of November, 1993. The top of the second page, item 5, "Humanitarian."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Muhamed Maric, deputy president of the Jablanica War Presidency said the majority of the refugees in the museum come from Doljani and included Muslims and Croats. There are 20 prisoners of war, total number not known, but all have free access to the town." Did both the Croat and Muslim refugees living in the museum have free access to the town of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And finally, Exhibit 664.5, an ECMM report for the 6th of November, 1993 -- excuse me, 8th of November. "M-1 visited the refugee and prisoner of war camp in the Jablanica museum where conditions were described as appalling. Over 600 refugees, Muslim and Croat, are accommodated in the building in addition to 41 Croat prisoners in five cells. There is an urgent need for supplies, in particular clothing." Sir, who was keeping humanitarian aid from coming to Jablanica at that time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The humanitarian aid would come through the territory of Herceg-Bosna. So all the obstructions that were put in its way was put by people from Herceg-Bosna. I believe that you have the report on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, as you just told us, that your own family lived in the Jablanica museum in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that they lived in the museum but that they lived in the basement of our building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Forgive me. And why were they living in the basement of the building at that time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my building which has 40 apartments -- so my building was hit by six artillery shells. And unfortunately the holes are still there. Nobody has repaired them. The things are as they were then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who was shelling Jablanica at that time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the HVO who shelled Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, I just have one question -- well, if we had time, I have many, but we don't. And you've been here a long time. I'm still not entirely clear about the diary. And forgive me for not being quick off the mark. Was the first document you saw the photocopy of the typed version, or was it the actual handwritten journal itself, or did you see both together?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And that brings me to, I think, a question that would logically follow: Are you aware or did you yourself photocopy the original handwritten journal at the time or close to the time that you first saw it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sihirlic, whom I've already mentioned, brought the photocopied blue-ink version, and obviously we first read that version, the original. Alojz was our colleague from work, and we were interested to see what he had written. That's why Zajko showed it to me immediately after he had made the first photocopy of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And in spite of my promises, a third follow-up question: So did you keep a photocopy of the handwritten journal as well as a photocopy of the typed version with you before any documents were handed to AID?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And did you give your photocopy of the handwritten journal to the OTP at any stage, or did you bring it with you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave it to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Idrizovic. I have a lot of questions to ask you, but I'm just going to have to read the documents and digest the evidence over the last two days. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you, witness, for coming here to give your evidence. I'm sorry for keeping you here for almost a week. Now you are free to go. The usher will show you out of the room. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since we are at a very late stage, if both parties have any documents to tender through this witness, I hope you could submit the written submissions. We will consider it at a later stage. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. It's Friday at 4.00. We'll next be in court on Monday morning presumably. We don't know who Witness X is and have received no summary, and we will not be prepared and we'll object to proceeding with cross-examination until we've had adequate time to have that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik has promised us to furnish us with some information about the latest development of Witness X.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my learned friend will have the complete information by the end of this day. We just didn't have the time to do it yesterday. I don't want to keep you any longer. We are all tired. I will act on your order today, and the rest of the information I will submit in the written form to both you and the Prosecutor today. I don't want to keep you any longer, and I don't want to give you any more information today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in order to satisfy my learned friend, that X cannot appear on Monday. My learned friend knows who is the witness on Monday. It cannot be X. I will inform you at a later stage about my Witness X. I don't want to tackle this issue in an open session, but I will send the information today, both through to my learned friend in the Prosecution and to you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric, are you on this subject or you are going to change to another subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was going to talk about the subject that has to do with your decision to carry out an expertise by an expert witness. Since I am planning to travel to Zagreb, I still don't have your decision, whether the rifle will be subject to an expert opinion. So what is your decision? I have to prepare that for my part of the rebuttal. I'm very short on time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll deal with it at a later stage. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. I wasn't finished --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. I really wasn't finished with the last issue. We can certainly go into private session for the name of the witness. But in any event, I'm concerned then, and I will ask counsel to please provide that information directly to the Office of the Prosecutor, because with all respect to the bureaucracy, when things are filed with the Registry, we sometimes don't get them for a day or two. If it reaches the Registry today, we probably won't get it until Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So I'd ask Mr. Krsnik, please. And Mr. President, I must also advise the Chamber, and I'm sure it's an unpleasant topic because of the hour. But before we rest our rebuttal case, we will need to advise you on some additional topics and Mr. Prelec. I'm not suggesting we do that now, but I am just alerting you that we have to cover that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have made a decision allowing Mr. Prelec to give testimony in the rebuttal proceedings within a limited scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And that's what I had to ask you -- to address the Chamber about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may do that Monday. Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I only have one short question: Will Mr. Prelec be testifying Monday morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Seric, I think this Chamber has already made a decision concerning the expert opinions of the wooden rifle already. If this Trial Chamber believes there's a need to call an expert witness, this Trial Chamber will do it proprio motu on that very issue. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you for the information. However, in order for -- to be able to prepare for this expert witness, I'm planning to go to Zagreb on Tuesday, and I don't know whether this expert witness is going to appear or not. I'm not an expert. I am just a lawyer from a small country, and I have to consult with other experts. I have to prepare myself for the possible testimony by that expert. And if you refuse our proposal, then my effort will be wasted. That's why I would like respectfully to be advised in due course. I don't insist that it should be today, but if that could be on Monday, I would be most grateful. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this Trial Chamber has made a decision that if we need the expert opinions, we'll call a witness proprio motu but not from your side. I think that's very clear. So there's no need for you to call any expert witness in this aspect. So having said that, we'll resume next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 4.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of October, 2002, at 9.30 a.m.
